This policy explains what personal information HI collects, why it is used and how it is protected. It also sets out your rights and the ways you can contact HI about your information or a privacy concern. On this page 01 Information we process 02 How it is used and shared 03 Your rights and contact 1. Who we are This website is operated by the International Youth Hostel Federation (IYHF), operating as Hostelling International (“HI”). Hostelling International is registered under the Charity Act in England & Wales (Registered Charity No. 1117014) and as a company (Registered No. 02250706). VAT Registration No. GB 196 641724. Our registered address is 7 Bell Yard, London, WC2A 2JR, UK. For the personal information described in this policy, HI is generally the data controller. Depending on the service you use, the relevant HI Member Association, hostel or service provider may also be an independent controller or processor. We will identify the relevant organisation where this is important to how your information is used. We have appointed a Data Protection Officer. You can contact the DPO at digital@hihostels.com or by post at our registered address, marked for the attention of the Data Protection Officer. 2. What this policy covers This policy explains how we collect, use, share and protect personal information when you: visit or use the new HI Hostels website contact us or make a group enquiry create or use an account, where that functionality is available book accommodation, buy membership or purchase another HI service through us subscribe to HI marketing communications. This policy should be read with our separate Cookie Policy and any booking, membership or service-specific terms and notices presented to you at the relevant time. 3. Information we collect Information you provide: depending on the service, we may collect your name, email address, phone number, country or place of residence, date of birth, postal address, account credentials, membership details, booking or enquiry details and the information you choose to include in a message to us. If you make a group enquiry, we may collect contact details such as your name, email address, country of residence and phone number so that we can pass the enquiry to the relevant hostel or Member Association and help them respond to you. If you buy membership or another service, we may collect the information needed to process the transaction, validate your membership and enable the relevant Association or hostel to provide the service. Information collected automatically: when you use the website, we may collect standard technical information such as your IP address, device and operating system, browser type, screen resolution, language, approximate location inferred from technical data, pages viewed, links followed and information about how you use the website. We use this to operate, secure, analyse and improve the website, subject to your choices and applicable law. We use cookies and similar technologies as explained in the Cookie Policy . Non-essential cookies will be used only where permitted and, where required, after you have given consent. Information from third parties: we may receive information from a social-media provider if you choose to sign in using a social-media profile, from a payment provider when you make a transaction, from a hostel or Member Association involved in providing your service, and from service providers that help us operate the website, bookings, communications or customer support. 4. How we use information and our legal bases We use personal information to: provide, administer and support bookings, memberships, group enquiries and other services pass necessary details to the relevant hostel or Member Association so it can provide the service, reserve accommodation, enter into an agreement with you and contact you about that service create and administer accounts, including enabling sign-in and displaying a social-media profile image where you have chosen that option process payments through a specialist payment provider respond to questions, requests and complaints send service messages, including messages intended to help complete an incomplete booking where applicable send HI or Member Association marketing where you have opted in, and manage your preferences and unsubscribes understand usage, diagnose problems, improve accessibility, security and performance, and develop our services prevent, detect and investigate fraud, abuse and other unlawful activity comply with legal obligations and establish, exercise or defend legal claims. Our legal bases may include performance of a contract or steps taken at your request before entering into a contract, compliance with a legal obligation, our legitimate interests, and your consent. Where we rely on consent, you can withdraw it at any time; withdrawal does not affect processing that took place before withdrawal. We do not make solely automated decisions based on information you submit that have legal or similarly significant effects on you. 5. Who we share information with We may share relevant information with: the hostel or Member Association responsible for providing the accommodation, membership or other service you request or purchase payment processors and other carefully selected suppliers that host, secure or operate our website and services email and marketing providers, such as Mailchimp, where you subscribe to HI communications analytics, security, customer-support and technology providers, where their use is permitted by law and consistent with your choices law-enforcement bodies, regulators, courts or other authorities where required by law or strictly necessary to prevent, detect or prosecute crime or fraud professional advisers or business partners where necessary to protect and defend our rights, property or services. We may also use anonymised or aggregated information for reporting, research and service improvement. We do not sell your personal information. Except as described in this policy, we will not share it without your permission unless we are legally entitled or required to do so. 6. Payments We use a specialist third-party payment processor. HI does not store or have full visibility of your payment-card details. The payment provider may offer secure card-storage functionality under its own terms and privacy notice. Where appropriate and authorised, HI may ask that provider to use stored payment details to pay for a service. 7. International transfers Some suppliers, hostels, Member Associations or other recipients may be located outside the UK or European Economic Area. Where personal information is transferred internationally, we use an appropriate lawful transfer mechanism and contractual or other safeguards required by applicable data-protection law. You can contact us for more information about the safeguards relevant to a particular transfer. 8. How long we keep information We keep personal information only for as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy, including to provide services, maintain business and financial records, resolve disputes, enforce agreements and meet legal obligations: account and marketing information is retained until you close the account or withdraw marketing consent, subject to necessary suppression records and legal obligations booking, membership and service information is retained for the period needed to provide the service and for a reasonable period afterwards for customer service, accounting, legal and audit purposes technical, analytics and cookie information is retained for the periods described in the Cookie Policy or the relevant provider’s settings. 9. Your rights Subject to applicable law, you may have the right to: ask for a copy of the personal information we hold about you ask us to correct inaccurate or incomplete information ask us to erase information, although we may need to retain some information where the law permits or requires it ask us to restrict processing object to processing based on legitimate interests, including direct marketing ask for portability of information you provided to us where applicable withdraw consent where processing is based on consent. To exercise your rights, contact digital@hihostels.com . Please explain your request and provide enough information for us to verify your identity. We normally respond within one month, although the law may allow an extension for complex requests. We may retain a minimal record of your request so that we can respect your preferences and demonstrate compliance. You can unsubscribe from marketing by using the link in our emails or contacting us. You can also manage non-essential cookies through the cookie settings on the website. If you are unhappy with how we have handled your personal information, please contact us first. You may also complain to the UK Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO): Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire SK9 5AF, UK telephone +44 303 123 1113 email casework@ico.org.uk. You may also have the right to contact another competent supervisory authority, depending on where you live or where the relevant processing takes place. 10. Children The website and services are not intended for children under 16 to use independently. If you are under 16, please stop using the service and ask a responsible adult for help. If we learn that we have collected personal information from someone under 16 without the consent required by law, we will take reasonable steps to obtain appropriate consent or delete the information. 11. Security We work to protect personal information using appropriate technical and organisational measures. Information submitted to the website is protected in transit using encryption such as SSL/TLS. We select service providers carefully and limit access to personal information to people and suppliers who need it for legitimate purposes. No internet transmission or storage system is completely secure. If we become aware of a personal-data breach affecting you, we will act and notify you or the relevant authority where required by law. 12. Changes to this policy We may update this policy to reflect changes to our services, technology, legal requirements or suppliers. We will publish the updated version on this page and change the effective date. Where required, we will give you additional notice or ask for consent. 13. Contact For all enquiries: digital@hihostels.com Postal contact: Data Protection Officer, International Youth Hostel Federation, 7 Bell Yard, London, WC2A 2JR, UK.
